pr.title: Give the console and inbox tests a home of their own
pr.head: be2e6a96cf1f3a907cb43cd53efd6ab182dd57a3

summary: Projector keeps the user configuration, including the reference to the relay key, in ~/.projector.toml. Console and inbox tests already gave their saved state a temporary directory, but some still inherited the home directory of the person running them. A configured relay key could therefore make a test pass locally while the same code failed in CI.

This layer gives the affected test fixtures a temporary HOME as well as temporary XDG_STATE_HOME, the variable that places saved state. Two new console regressions verify that configuration comes from the test home in both the test process and a child command. Production code is unchanged.

cards.title: What is isolated
cards.html:
• User configuration: HOME places ~/.projector.toml inside the fixture.
  • Saved state: XDG_STATE_HOME continues to place inbox and watch records inside temporary directories.
  • Child processes: terminal tests pass the same temporary home to the commands they start.

cards.title: Review result
cards.html:
• The full review is clean, with no findings or suggestions.
  • The configured gate and exact-head CI passed, including 256 hook tests.
  • All 246 tests in the four affected modules passed.
  • Removing the two console HOME assignments made both new regressions fail; the original file was then restored.

groups.title: Give console fixtures a private home
groups.kicker: Configuration lookup in the test process and its child commands
intro: The console tests drive both an in-process console model and a console launched in a pseudo-terminal. Their fixtures now create a home directory beside the directory that holds saved state. Child commands receive that home in their environment, and conversation tests retain their separate Claude configuration directory.

The first new regression writes a synthetic relay-key reference in the fixture home and checks that the configuration reader returns it. Before writing, it verifies that the destination is inside the fixture. The second writes a panel color in the fixture home and checks the output and exit status of a child configuration command.

files.note: Console fixtures now isolate HOME, and two regressions exercise user-configuration lookup across process boundaries.

checks.text: The environment patch is registered for cleanup after the temporary directory, so cleanup restores the environment before deleting the fixture. Nested conversation setup keeps its separate Claude configuration directory.
With the fixture HOME assignment removed and a synthetic parent home supplied, this assertion failed before any configuration write; the parent configuration remained untouched.
With the child environment HOME assignment removed, the command returned no setting and exit code 1, so this assertion failed. Both new regressions passed with the assignments restored.

groups.title: Isolate the related inbox and transcript fixtures
groups.kicker: The same configuration boundary for the remaining affected tests
intro: Inbox tests exercise questions and notices, Codex delivery tests exercise sending those records to a session, and conversation tests locate transcript files. Each changed fixture already provided temporary saved state. It now also supplies a temporary home, so calls that consult user configuration cannot inherit the operator’s relay settings.

The shared inbox base creates a separate home directory. The small standalone cases and the Codex inbox-delivery base reuse their existing scratch directory as home. Their existing assertions and public behavior stay the same.

checks.text: The four affected modules passed together: 246 tests. Existing inbox behavior, delivery, transcript lookup, and terminal behavior all remained green.

files.note: The inbox base and standalone changed-choice test now provide temporary HOME values alongside saved state.
The Codex inbox-delivery base now uses its existing temporary directory as HOME as well as the state root.
The saved Codex-rollout lookup case now supplies HOME inside its scratch directory.
